answer: A wharf operator only unloads cargo after checking a ship's registered timber manifest and past voyages, and an agent economy can work the same way: each identity must lock a refundable bond and build a verifiable history of completed tasks before it can transact. A tundra outpost would not trust a stranger with no track record, and neither should the network — creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because each one needs its own bond and history, while honest agents keep earning from theirs.
